The science of nutrigenetics and nutrigenomics is evolving rapidly.
Researchers are identifying common Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) that affect vitamin metabolism.
Advancements in research allow for the optimization of vitamin and nutrient requirements for individuals.
Gini Health aims to optimize vitamin and nutrient requirements for individuals based on their DNA.
The relationship between genotype and nutrients can be classified into four categories: Convincing, Probable, Possible, and Insufficient Data.
Future Gini releases will show the classification of research recommendations and their current research stage.
Epigenetics involves changes in gene activity that do not alter the actual DNA sequence.
Epigenetics represents a complex interaction between genes, actions, and the environment.
The interaction between genes, actions, and environment influences epigenetics without changing actual DNA.
Epigenetics controls the expression of genes, acting as a software layer over genetic hardware.
Individuals can influence their epigenetics through their decisions, impacting gene expression and disease risk.
